summary: Forest Service two-story lookout on Leviathan Peak, Alpine County, CA; register says 1957 build, a 1958 Reno item says permanent construction began Oct 1958; reached by 4WD road to a gate.

facts.design: Two-story: concrete-block ground floor with a cab and catwalk; an R4 adaptation of a flat-roof design similar to R6. A 1958 item describes a glass cab on a cinder-block base about ten feet high, built for a man and wife lookout team.

staffing.status: not recently staffed, per a third-party photo site (undated page)

access.note: Public road ends at a locked gate about a quarter mile from the tower; the last section is for service vehicles, per a third-party guide. The summit also has transmission facilities.

visit.trail_note: 4WD recommended on Leviathan Peak Road (Forest Road 31057); the road is closed in winter and usually opens early April to late November, per a third-party guide. The sources read do not say whether the cab may be entered.

events.note: Two fishermen at Topaz Lake spotted a fire on the West Walker River; this led to considering a lookout on the peak
Register gives 1957 as the build year; conflicts with the 1958 article
Temporary lookout facilities established atop the peak in 1957 and 1958 (Reno Evening Gazette item, Oct. 20, 1958)
Construction of the permanent station began the week of Oct. 20, 1958 (Reno Evening Gazette item); the register's 1957 date is disputed
Registered June 4, 1998; nominated by Mark Swift; US 282, CA 16

Volunteer schedule in the FFLA California South 2024 report lists an August 14 evaluation of Leviathan Lookout, with a report to be submitted to Jeff Baggett. The schedule does not confirm the evaluation was done.
August 2024 photo on the register page shows the lookout standing

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1957. A Reno Evening Gazette item dated October 20, 1958 says temporary facilities stood on the peak in 1957 and 1958 and that construction of the permanent station began that week. Both are reported; the register's date may refer to the temporary facilities.
A third-party guide calls the lookout old and abandoned; an undated photo site says it is in good shape. Neither is an official status; the register shows it standing in August 2024.

notes_for_editor: Brief said the 2024 evaluation was done and a report submitted; the source is a volunteer schedule (Evaluate ... Submit report), so the story says it is listed, not done. Build year conflict (1957 register vs Oct 1958 article) is reported, not corrected. Staffing comes from an undated photo site. Access and winter closure come from a third-party 4WD guide, not a Forest Service source; confirm with the Carson Ranger District or the Humboldt-Toiyabe MVUM before relying on it. The brief's registration date and NHLR record matched the page read. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the guide says 4WD is recommended, not required, and the story now says so; the photo page's staffing statement is undated and the story now says the page gives no date for it. Pages read: 6 (2 of them the same FFLA PDF with different greps) plus 2 web searches.
